typed: I look for Calbert Oakward around the village. Maybe he's at the gate, since he's the captain. I go there and ask him about the omen.
note: The output was confusing. It says I reached Calbert and that it worked, then says he isn't in Barrowburn but can be found in the village today. That contradicts itself. I also didn't get to see the omen or the jetties described, so the scene feels thin.

typed: Yes. I lean in and keep my voice low. "Calbert, you've been staring at that seam since I walked up. What do you actually think it means? And have you told the aldermen?"
note: The narration was a bit muddled. It mixed the scene description with Calbert's reaction, and it never said what the omen looks like. The earlier "not in Barrowburn and can be found in the village" line was confusing too. Otherwise it's fine.

typed: "A friend, Calbert. We've known each other long enough. I'm not sent by anyone. I just want to know what you're really thinking." I hold his gaze. "What happened to your eye? And what do you think the aldermen would do if you told them?"
note: Good NPC reply with some suspense. The earlier "moved within Barrowburn... not in Barrowburn and can be found in the village" message was garbled. The scene text also dropped a bit of the omen description.

Odds are clear (85%) and the stakes are readable. Calbert's repeated "Mark me" and the identical "doesn't look at the notice post or ruts" lines feel repetitive. Terms like "closed door, S2" and "Reach: limited" are jargon I don't understand.

The near-miss menu is clear. Options 1 and 3 have the same cost text, so it's hard to tell why I'd pick "succeed and pay" with the closed door over letting it fail. Calbert's "Mark me" line is repeated, and he is stonewalling a lot.

typed: I follow him toward the gate and ask quietly, "Fine, keep your secrets. Then who at the gate saw the omen first? And who put up that new bill on the notice post?"
note: Menu worked, but Calbert repeats "Mark me" and refuses again. Paying the drain cost gave no new information, so it felt like a wasted price. The "human turns" phrasing is odd for a human NPC. No stated way to see the drain I took.

typed: I offer him a deal. "I'll bring you what the aldermen say to me, word for word. But first, give me one true thing now as good faith. Who else at the gate might talk to me about that bill?"
note: Calbert keeps repeating the same refusals, and the scene text keeps mentioning the notice post and ruts. The prompt "What do you offer him?" has no menu or suggested options, so I'm not sure what offers are possible. The narration also says he is "in the doorway" while we're on the jetties, which is a bit inconsistent.

Mostly fine. The narration repeats the same stock details (cold, wet planks, "does not look at the notice post"). Calbert's "Yes," reply doesn't answer my question, and a woman is hinted at with no name. Pronoun and place slips: Evbert is "she" in the offer text but "he" elsewhere. The doorway and jetties scene is also muddled, since there was no door. The Enter default is Withdraw, which is a bit easy to hit by mistake.

typed: I walk over to the woman with her shoulders drawn in and say quietly, "Morning. I'm Evbert. Do you know anything about that new bill on the post?"
note: The Enter default let the trade fail without a fuss, which was fine. Two near misses in a row at 9 vs 10 felt a bit unlucky. Calbert's repeated "hands at his belt" and "cart ruts" lines are getting repetitive. I also never learned the woman's name.

typed: "I don't want to get you in trouble. Is there somewhere else we could talk, away from the gate, maybe later today? I'll keep your name out of it."
note: Good scene, but the woman is unnamed. The captain keeps interrupting. The near-miss prompt after the trade came right before I typed a free action, so I'm not sure whether that choice was resolved.

The woman already said "Yes" to meeting, then the game offers a 50% roll with a closed-door risk to get what she just agreed to. That's a bit confusing. Otherwise the offer text is clear. The Calbert scenes repeated the same wet planks and wind imagery.

typed: "Thank you, Norhild. Where and when? Tell me a place and an hour, and I'll come alone."
note: Fine. Her name appeared only after the roll, which was a bit abrupt. The "later today" is vague, so I'm not sure a meeting is actually set. Good tension overall.

typed: I press her gently. "Just a place, Norhild. Somewhere quiet. The boathouse, the chapel, wherever you'd feel safe. And what should I call you if anyone asks?"
note: Fine. The previous reply repeated my line back to me before the scene moved. Norhild's name appeared without being introduced, which was a bit abrupt. I liked the near-miss choice and the odds shown up front.
The offer screen is clear, but the stakes text is dense. The 50% odds for a gentle follow-up question feel a bit harsh. The menu's default is Withdraw, which makes it easy to back out by accident.
